11 A uniform beam of mass 1.4 kg is pivoted at P as shown. The beam has a length of 0.60 m and P
is 0.20 m from one end. Loads of 3.0 kg and 6.0 kg are suspended 0.35 m and 0.15 m from the
pivot as shown.
0.20 m
0.40 m
0.15 m
0.35 m
P
3.0 kg
6.0 kg
centre of beam
of mass 1.4 kg
What is the torque that must be applied to the beam in order to maintain it in equilibrium?
A
0.010 N m
B
0.10 N m
C
0.29 N m
D
2.8 N m

hints: Notice the three distances from P: $3.0 \text{ kg}$ at $0.35 \text{ m}$ left, $6.0 \text{ kg}$ at $0.15 \text{ m}$ right, and the beam centre $0.10 \text{ m}$ left of P because the $0.60 \text{ m}$ centre is $0.30 \text{ m}$ from the left end while P is $0.40 \text{ m}$ from the left end.
Recall torque about P is $F \times d$ with $F = mg$, so each weight gives an opposing moment and the beam weight also contributes because its centre is not over P.
Combine clockwise and anticlockwise $mgd$ terms to find the net $\text{kg m}$ imbalance first, then multiply by $g \approx 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to get the balancing torque in $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: Locate all weights relative to P. Left side: $3.0 \text{ kg}$ at $0.35 \text{ m}$ and beam $1.4 \text{ kg}$ at $0.10 \text{ m}$ left, since centre is $0.30 \text{ m}$ from the end and P is $0.20 \text{ m}$ from the right end. Right side: $6.0 \text{ kg}$ at $0.15 \text{ m}$.
State the principle of moments: for equilibrium the sum of moments about P plus any applied torque must be zero, so applied torque $= $ net $mgd$ imbalance.
Calculate mass moments. Anticlockwise: $3.0 \times 0.35 + 1.4 \times 0.10 = 1.05 + 0.14 = 1.19 \text{ kg m}$. Clockwise: $6.0 \times 0.15 = 0.90 \text{ kg m}$.
Find net imbalance: $1.19 - 0.90 = 0.29 \text{ kg m}$ anticlockwise. Convert to torque by multiplying by $g$: $0.29 \times 9.81 \approx 2.84 \text{ N m}$.
An applied torque of about $2.8 \text{ N m}$ in the opposite clockwise sense is needed to cancel this. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 280. This comes from an arithmetic or $g$ error after finding the $0.29 \text{ kg m}$ imbalance.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 28. This is close to using $g \approx 1$ or misplacing a decimal when converting the $0.29 \text{ kg m}$ moment to $\text{N m}$.

C.explanation: This is the unbalanced mass moment $0.29 \text{ kg m}$, found from $(3.0 \times 0.35 + 1.4 \times 0.10 - 6.0 \times 0.15)$. It omits multiplication by $g$ to get torque.

D.explanation: The net moment about P is $9.81 \times 0.29 \approx 2.8 \text{ N m}$ anticlockwise, so an equal clockwise torque of $2.8 \text{ N m}$ restores equilibrium.
